s: At MC14 (2026), along with which group did India seek a permanent shield for public stockholding programmes like the NFSA?
x: India and the African Group sought a permanent solution, which MC14 did not deliver.

s: The Peace Clause shields public stockholding even if it breaches which of the following?
x: It shields developing-country PSH for food security from disputes even if de minimis or AMS limits are breached.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Peace Clause:
1. It applies only to existing programmes and traditional staples.
2. It requires notification by the country using it.
3. It was made permanent at MC13.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It is limited to existing programmes and traditional staples and needs notification; no permanent solution came at MC13 or MC14.

s: To what did WTO dispute DS456, which India lost to the US in 2016, relate?
x: DS456 concerned solar cells; DS541 (MEIS, SEZ, EOU) went against India in 2019 and the ICT panel ruled against India in 2023.

s: What did the WTO dispute brought by Brazil, Australia and Guatemala against India concern?
x: The sugar dispute concerned India's cane prices and export subsidies; the panel ruled against India in 2021 and the matter was appealed.

s: Along with IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform, what did the BRICS New Delhi Declaration (September 2026) seek?
o: Restoration of the WTO Appellate Body
Replacement of the WTO by a BRICS trade body
Merger of the IMF and the World Bank
x: The declaration sought IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform and restoration of the two-tier WTO dispute-settlement system, i.e. the Appellate Body.

s: Since when has the WTO Appellate Body been non-functional?
x: The Appellate Body stopped functioning in December 2019 as the US blocked appointments; India has not joined the EU-led MPIA (2020).

s: Who blocked appointments to the WTO Appellate Body, making it non-functional since December 2019?
x: The US blocked appointments, leaving the Appellate Body non-functional since December 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA):
1. It is an EU-led stop-gap set up in 2020.
2. India has joined it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The MPIA is an EU-led 2020 stop-gap for the paralysed Appellate Body; India has not joined it.

s: What did WTO dispute DS541, ruled against India in 2019, concern?
x: DS541 (US) was on export subsidies under MEIS, SEZ and EOU schemes; DS456 was solar cells.

s: Who brought the WTO dispute over India's duties on phones and ICT goods?
x: The ICT tariffs dispute (EU, Japan, Taiwan) went against India in 2023; Brazil, Australia and Guatemala brought the sugar case.

s: Which pair of WTO agreements is identified as the only two new agreements concluded in the last 30 years?
o: TFA and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only two new WTO agreements concluded in the last 30 years.

s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the first WTO agreement with which objective?
x: The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.

s: What happened at MC14 to Phase 2 of the WTO fisheries subsidies negotiations on overcapacity and overfishing?
o: Deferred to the General Council in Geneva
Referred to the Dispute Settlement Body
x: Phase 2 was not concluded at MC14; it was sent to the General Council in Geneva.

s: What is India's main concern about plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and the E-Commerce Agreement?
o: May fragment the WTO by moving away from consensus
x: India fears plurilaterals may fragment the WTO by weakening consensus-based multilateralism.

s: Which of the following is NOT prohibited under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: Subsidies for fishing on unregulated high seas
Subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
Subsidies for fishing in overfished stocks, unless rebuilding conditions apply
x: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. Aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.

s: Indian fisher bodies, including Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, have sought which approach to WTO fisheries-subsidy rules?
x: The rules matter to Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, and Indian fisher bodies have sought a fisher-centric approach to implementing them.

s: When did the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, adopted in 2022, enter into force?
x: Adopted at MC12 in 2022, it entered into force in September 2025.

s: When did India become the 123rd WTO member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance for the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
x: India deposited its Instrument of Acceptance in July 2026, becoming the 123rd WTO member to do so.

s: When did the WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, in place since 1998, lapse?
x: The moratorium lapsed for the first time on 31 March 2026.

s: Which of the following does the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies exempt?
x: AFS covers marine wild capture; aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: FDI – Lasting interest with management control, generally 10% or more of equity
FPI – Investment in securities below 10% of a company's equity
Automatic Route – Foreign investment requiring prior government approval
P-Note – Offshore derivative instrument issued by a registered FPI
x: The automatic route needs no prior government approval.

s: What does foreign direct investment under the automatic route require?
o: No prior approval, but post-facto reporting to the RBI
Prior approval of the concerned Ministry
x: The automatic route needs no prior RBI or Government approval, only post-facto reporting to the RBI.

s: Which approach does India's FDI policy follow?
x: India follows a negative-list approach; FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and DPIIT is the nodal department.

s: Under which Ministry is DPIIT, the nodal department for FDI policy and data?
x: DPIIT is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; its FIF Portal has been part of the NSWS since August 2022.

s: When was the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) abolished?
x: FIPB ended in June 2017; applications now go to ministries through the FIF Portal under DPIIT.

s: After the FIPB's abolition, through which platform are Government-route FDI proposals filed for ministry approval?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
x: Government-route proposals need prior approval of the concerned ministry via the FIF Portal, part of the National Single Window System since August 2022.

s: Which law did the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 replace?
x: FEMA 1999 replaced FERA 1973; the RBI regulates ECBs under FEMA.

s: Which of the following about India's FDI policy is NOT correct?
o: Caps were raised after 2014 in defence, insurance and pension.
The e-commerce marketplace model permits 100% FDI via the automatic route.
All sectors are exclusively on the automatic route.
More than 90% of sectors are on the automatic route.
x: Some sectors still need the Government route, though over 90% are on the automatic route.

s: Up to what limit is FDI in brownfield pharmaceutical projects permitted under the automatic route?
x: Brownfield pharma allows 74% automatically (approval beyond), greenfield pharma and medical devices 100% automatically.

s: In which year was the FDI limit in the insurance sector raised to 74%?
x: The insurance FDI cap went from 26% to 49% in 2015, 74% in 2021 and 100% in 2025.

s: Up to what limit is FDI permitted in the telecom sector in India?
x: Telecom allows 100% FDI through the automatic route; 74% automatic is the defence limit and 51% Government route is multi-brand retail.

s: Up to what limit is FDI in the defence sector permitted under the automatic route?
x: Defence allows 74% FDI under the automatic route and up to 100% through the Government route.

s: What is the foreign investment cap in private-sector banks in India?
x: Private banks allow 74% (49% automatic); public-sector banks allow 20% via the Government route.

s: What is the FDI limit and route for multi-brand retail trading in India?
x: Multi-brand retail allows up to 51% FDI only through the Government route (in practice treated as barred). 100% automatic applies to single-brand retail, telecom and e-commerce marketplaces; 74% automatic is the defence limit; 49% automatic is the automatic slab within the private-bank and scheduled-airline caps.

s: Where is the headquarters of IRDAI?
x: IRDAI is headquartered in Hyderabad; Budget 2025-26 raised insurance FDI to 100%, and insurance is in the Union List.

s: What is the cap on foreign investment in public sector banks in India?
x: Public sector banks allow 20% through the Government route; private banks allow 74% (49% automatic).

s: For foreign investors other than NRIs, up to what limit is FDI in scheduled civil aviation allowed under the automatic route?
x: Scheduled civil aviation allows 100% FDI, of which 49% is automatic; NRIs may invest 100% under the automatic route.

s: In which year was FDI in single-brand retail first eased, up to 51%?
x: Single-brand retail was first opened up to 51% in 2006; in 2012 it went to 100% and multi-brand retail to 51%.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI in insurance:
1. The cap was raised from 26% to 49% in 2015.
2. It was raised to 74% with effect from 19 May 2021.
3. Insurance is listed in Entry 47 of the State List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are true. Statement 3 is false: insurance is Entry 47 of the Union List.

s: Up to what limit and by which route is FDI permitted in trading, including e-commerce, of food products made in India?
x: Trading of food products made in India, including through e-commerce, allows 100% FDI under the Government route.

s: What is the FDI limit in the insurance sector after the Union Budget 2025-26?
x: Budget 2025-26 raised the insurance FDI cap from 74% to 100% (automatic route), with the entire premium to be invested in India.

s: In which year was the FDI limit in private sector banks raised from 49% to 74%?
x: FDI in private banks was 49% (2003) and was raised to 74% in 2004.

s: In which e-commerce model is 100% FDI under the automatic route allowed in India?
x: The marketplace model allows 100% FDI through the automatic route; FDI in the inventory model is generally barred, apart from a later export-related relaxation.

s: In July 2026, in which situation was FDI in inventory-based e-commerce allowed?
o: The inventory is used for exporting domestically manufactured goods.
The platform operates only as a marketplace.
The inventory is owned entirely by foreign companies for domestic resale.
The inventory is used to sell imported goods in the domestic market.
x: The July 2026 relaxation allowed inventory-based e-commerce FDI where the inventory is used to export domestically manufactured goods.

s: Which of the following is NOT a sector prohibited for FDI in India?
x: Railway operations are prohibited except for permitted activities, but railway infrastructure is included among sectors permitting 100% automatic FDI. Lottery business, chit funds and atomic energy are prohibited sectors.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI in India:
1. Railway infrastructure allows 100% FDI under the automatic route.
2. Railway operations are prohibited for FDI, except permitted activities.
3. Chit funds and Nidhi companies allow 100% FDI under the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are true: only railway operations are barred. Statement 3 is false: chit funds and Nidhi companies are prohibited sectors.

s: In the manufacture of which of the following is FDI prohibited in India?
x: Manufacture of cigars and cigarettes of tobacco is a prohibited sector; medical devices and pharma allow 100% automatic, defence 74% automatic.

s: In which of the following is FDI prohibited in India?
x: Trading in TDRs is in the prohibited list; medical devices, railway infrastructure and ports allow 100% automatic FDI.

s: Of what is Hyundai's facility at Sriperumbudur an example?
x: Greenfield investment creates a new facility; brownfield means acquiring an existing business (e.g., Vodafone-Hutchison Essar).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about FDI?
o: Gross FDI consists entirely of fresh capital.
It is associated with stable capital.
It can help finance the current account deficit.
x: Gross FDI may include accounting changes and is not entirely fresh capital.

s: How is foreign investment by a person resident outside India in an unlisted Indian company treated?
o: FPI, if the stake is below 10%
FPI, whatever the size of the stake
FDI, whatever the size of the stake
x: Any stake in an unlisted company counts as FDI; the 10% line applies only to listed companies.

s: Of what is Vodafone's acquisition of Hutchison Essar an example?
x: Brownfield FDI is investment through acquisition of an existing firm, as in Vodafone-Hutchison Essar; greenfield means a new facility.

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes FDI from FPI?
o: FDI is always debt; FPI is always equity
FDI is generally long-term and may carry management control; FPI is liquid and short-term
FDI is regulated only by SEBI; FPI only by the RBI
FDI is limited to unlisted firms; FPI to government securities
x: FDI is generally long-term and may bring management control and technology, while FPI is liquid, potentially short-term 'hot money'.

s: Which of the following about the SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 is NOT correct?
o: They kept QFIs outside the FPI framework
They brought FIIs under the FPI framework
They brought sub-accounts under the FPI framework
They unified several foreign investor categories as FPIs
x: The 2019 Regulations brought FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs together under the FPI framework, so QFIs were not kept outside.

s: For a listed company, at what equity holding is foreign investment generally classified as FDI?
x: Under the threshold associated with the Arvind Mayaram Committee classification, an equity holding of 10% or more in a listed company is treated as FDI. Holdings below 10% are classified as portfolio investment.

s: In which year was Foreign Portfolio Investment opened to India?
x: FPI was opened in 1992 and is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, along with the RBI.

s: Which of the following about FDI and FPI is NOT correct?
o: FDI can bring technology and management skills
FDI targets specific sectors or enterprises
FDI is generally more volatile than FPI
FPI is mainly investment in securities
x: FDI is more stable and long-term; it is FPI that is the more volatile flow.

s: On whose recommendation is the 10% threshold separating FDI from FPI based?
x: The Arvind Mayaram Committee set the 10% line: 10% or more in a listed company is FDI, below it FPI.

s: Foreign Institutional Investment (FII) is a form of which type of investment?
x: FII is portfolio investment, whereas FDI is direct investment in enterprises or sectors.

s: With which body must Foreign Portfolio Investors in India be registered?
x: FPIs must register with SEBI and are overseen by SEBI and the RBI.

s: Where in Andhra Pradesh did Google announce a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre?
x: Google's $15 billion AI data centre is in Visakhapatnam; AP's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets at least $10 billion FDI.

s: What was India's net FDI in FY 2024-25?
x: In FY 2024-25 gross FDI was $81 billion but net FDI only $353 million.

s: What share of India's FDI in FY 2024-25 came from Singapore, the top investor country?
x: Singapore contributed about 30% of FDI in FY 2024-25, followed by Mauritius (17%) and the United States (11%).

s: Why may net FDI remain weak despite high gross inflows?
o: Exclusion of services from net FDI
Profit repatriation, outward FDI and PE/VC exits
Exclusion of all foreign equity from net FDI
Deduction of imports from gross FDI
x: Net FDI is reduced by profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and PE/VC exits.

s: What was India's record gross FDI in FY 2025-26?
x: FY 2025-26 saw record gross FDI of $94.6 billion, with net FDI of $7.6 billion.

s: Which of the following correctly gives the order of the top three states by FDI during the first half of FY 2025-26?
x: Maharashtra ranked first, Karnataka second and Tamil Nadu third during the first half of FY 2025-26.

s: Why has the debate on gross and net FDI in India involved the Chief Economic Adviser and critics?
o: net FDI excludes all foreign equity inflows
gross FDI may include accounting changes and therefore may not reflect fresh capital fully
manufacturing FDI is always higher than services FDI
gross FDI and net FDI always represent identical flows
x: The debate arises because gross FDI can include accounting changes, whereas the amount of fresh capital may be considerably lower, as reflected in the difference between gross and net figures.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, services accounted for what share of FDI during FY 2023-FY 2025?
x: Services accounted for 80.2% of FDI during FY 2023-FY 2025. Information and communication alone accounted for 25.8%.

s: Which RBI regional office received the largest cumulative FDI during April 2000–March 2015?
x: Mumbai received the most, followed by New Delhi, Chennai and Bangalore.

s: In which year did India's net FDI reach its peak of $44.0 billion?
x: Net FDI peaked at $44.0 bn in 2020-21; in 2024-25 it was only $353 mn.

s: How much FDI did Andhra Pradesh receive in FY 2025-26?
x: AP drew $608.59 mn in FY 2025-26, up from $233.14 mn in 2024-25 and $92.13 mn in 2023-24; $250.67 mn was the metallurgical share.

s:
Consider the following statements about FDI in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Metallurgical industries led FDI inflows in FY 2025-26.
2. Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets FDI of at least $10 billion.
3. FDI in FY 2025-26 was lower than in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are true. Statement 3 is false: AP's FDI rose from $233.14 mn in 2024-25 to $608.59 mn in FY 2025-26.

s: According to the World Investment Report 2026, which country was both the largest recipient and the largest investor of FDI in 2025?
x: WIR 2026 reports global FDI up 6% to $1.6 trillion, with the US the largest recipient and source; India is the largest recipient in South Asia.

s: Which country was the third-largest source of FDI into India in FY 2024-25?
x: In FY25, Singapore (30%) led, followed by Mauritius (17%) and the US (11%).

s: Which sector had the largest share (25.8%) within services FDI inflows during FY23-FY25?
x: Services took 80.2% of FDI in FY23-FY25, with information and communication at 25.8%.

s: Why did India mainly opt out of the RCEP in 2019?
o: The exclusion of ASEAN countries from the bloc
China's market dominance and the widening trade deficit with China
A requirement to withdraw from the WTO
A ban on Indian exports to Australia
x: India withdrew over China's market dominance, its rising trade deficit with China and risks to farm, dairy and small industries.

s: When did the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) come into force?
x: The India-UAE CEPA came into force on 1 May 2022; the Australia ECTA followed on 29 December 2022.

s: Which of the following agreement–partner pairs is correctly matched?
x: India's ECTA is with Australia; TEPA is with EFTA, CETA with the UK and CEPA with the UAE.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's trade agreements:
1. The India-EFTA TEPA came into force on 1 October 2025.
2. The India-UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: TEPA (signed 10 March 2024) came into force on 1 October 2025, and CETA (signed 24 July 2025) on 15 July 2026.

s: In which year did the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) among the eight SAARC members come into force?
x: SAFTA came into force in 2006; SAPTA was signed in 1993 and came into force in 1995.

s: How many countries signed the RCEP on 15 November 2020?
x: RCEP was signed by 15 members: ASEAN 10 plus China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the RCEP?
x: India opted out of RCEP in 2019; Australia, New Zealand and South Korea are among its 15 members.

s: In which year was India's trade deficit with China, a key reason for leaving RCEP, $53.5 billion?
x: The deficit with China was $53.5 bn in 2018-19, when India opted out, and rose to $99.2 bn by 2024-25.

s: In which year did the ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement in goods come into force?
x: The ASEAN-India FTA in goods came into force in 2010.

s: When did the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) come into force?
x: RCEP was signed by 15 members on 15 November 2020 and came into force on 1 January 2022.

s: External commercial borrowings, trade credit and NRI deposits are all forms of which of the following?
x: Foreign capital in India includes FDI, trade credit, NRI deposits and ECBs.

s: Which of the following is correctly classified as debt capital?
x: External commercial borrowing is debt capital. FDI and FPI are non-debt forms, while ADRs represent equity raised abroad through depository receipts.

s: How are ADRs and GDRs counted in balance of payments data?
x: ADRs and GDRs represent equity raised abroad through depository receipts and are counted as portfolio investment in balance of payments data.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wholly owned Indian subsidiary of a foreign company – FPI
Foreign fund buying 5% of a listed Indian company – FDI
x: A P-Note is an offshore derivative instrument. A wholly owned subsidiary is FDI, a 5% listed stake is FPI, and a masala bond is a rupee bond issued abroad.

s: When did FCNR(B) deposits replace FCNR(A) deposits?
x: FCNR(B), a fixed deposit held in foreign currency, replaced FCNR(A) on 15 May 1993.

s: What is a rupee-denominated bond issued abroad by an Indian entity called?
x: A masala bond is a rupee bond issued abroad; FCCBs are debt and GDRs are equity raised abroad.

s: Who issues a Participatory Note (P-Note), giving an overseas investor exposure to Indian stocks?
x: P-Notes are issued by registered FIIs/FPIs to overseas investors, who gain exposure to Indian shares without registering with SEBI.

s: How is a Foreign Currency Convertible Bond (FCCB) classified among forms of foreign capital?
x: ECBs, trade credit and FCCBs are debt forms of foreign capital.

s: Who regulates External Commercial Borrowings?
x: FEMA, 1999 replaced FERA, 1973, and ECBs are regulated by the RBI under FEMA.

s: What is India's target weight in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index?
x: India entered the JP Morgan EM bond index with a target weight of 10%, which is expected to attract passive bond inflows.

s: Under the General Route, what is the overall FPI limit in outstanding Central Government securities?
x: The General Route limit is 6% of Central and 2% of State Government securities.

s: By which of the following are FPI flows into India significantly influenced?
o: US Federal Reserve interest rates and global risk appetite
x: US interest rates and global risk sentiment strongly drive FPI flows; a flight to safety can cause outflows.

s: Under the General Route, FPIs may hold up to what share of outstanding State Government securities?
x: The General Route limits are 6% of Central G-secs and 2% of State securities; 15% is the corporate bond limit.

s: What were the FPI outflows in FY 2025-26?
x: FPI outflows in FY26 were about ₹2.2 lakh crore; ₹24,829 crore was the equity outflow in May 2026 alone.

s: Under the RBI framework of November 2024, an FPI holding above what share of a listed company's equity can be reclassified as FDI?
x: An FPI stake above 10% of a listed company can be reclassified as FDI, matching the 10% FDI-FPI line.

s: Which of the following countries is NOT covered by Press Note 3 (April 2020)?
x: Press Note 3 covers land-border countries (China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan); Sri Lanka shares no land border.

s: Under the March 2026 amendment to Press Note 3, up to what level of Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership may a foreign firm use the automatic route from 1 May 2026?
x: Firms with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership up to 10% may use the automatic route, provided they are not registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country.

s: Under Press Note 3 (April 2020), through which route must all FDI from a country sharing a land border with India come?
x: Press Note 3 requires Government approval for all FDI from land-border countries; China is not named in it.

s: Under the March 2026 amendment to Press Note 3, as per which of the following is 'beneficial owner' defined?
x: The amendment uses the beneficial-owner definition of the Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Rules, 2005.
